Leg.description: Leg is one OS check's leg, by its record's name.

leg.description: Leg is the check's own record of its leg.

name.description: Name is the leg's record name: mac, bsd or win.

LegRecord.description: LegRecord is one check's record of its machine's run.

commit.description: Commit is the commit whose tree the leg tested. A leg tests the tree git archive makes of that commit, never the working tree, so it is clean by construction and the record has no clean field: a merge compares only this commit with the run's.

error.description: Error is why the leg did not pass, or what went wrong after its tests passed (a box that could not be put back).

kind.description: Kind is always leg. Known values: leg. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

os.description: OS is the machine's operating system, as the check names it.

packages.description: Packages are the import paths the leg tested.

runs.description: Runs are the testgate records the machine wrote, in the order its passes ran.

schema.description: Schema is the leg record's version (LegSchema).

seconds.description: Seconds is how long the leg took.

started.description: Started is when the leg began.

step.description: Step is where a leg that did not pass stopped. Known values: settings, box, commit, reachable, ready, ship, test. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

target.description: Target is the machine: its device or ssh name.

tool.description: Tool is the check that ran the leg: maccheck, bsdcheck or wincheck.

verdict.description: Verdict is flakegate's: pass, fail, not-run (the tests never ran), or error (they ran and their outcome is unknown). Known values: pass, fail, error, not-run. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

Pass.description: Pass is one testgate pass on this machine, by its record's name.

name.description: Name is the pass's record name: fast, repeat or containers.

run.description: Run is the pass's own testgate record.

Problem.description: Problem is one reason a report cannot simply be read as its records say.

code.description: Code is what kind of problem it is, stable for a tool to act on. Known values: unreadable, unknown-kind, unknown-schema, unknown-value, missing, gate-failed, gate-disagrees, interrupted, stale, dirty. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

detail.description: Detail says what happened, for a person.

record.description: Record is the record file or the expected part of the run it is about; absent for a problem about the run as a whole.

Run.description: Run is one testgate run's record.

arch.description: Arch is the architecture it ran on (GOARCH).

clean.description: Clean is true when the working tree had no uncommitted changes as pr-check began (testgate -clean yes). A stamped record without it ran over code that is in no commit.

commit.description: Commit is the commit pr-check began at, which the run tested (testgate -commit); absent on a record nobody stamped, which a merge cannot tie to any commit.

coverage.description: Coverage is each package's statement coverage, in percent.

error.description: Error is why a run could not reach a verdict, or why it failed beyond its failures (too many to re-run).

failures.description: Failures are each failure go test reported, with how the run judged it.

kind.description: Kind is always testgate. Known values: testgate. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

label.description: Label is the run's go test arguments, as testgate prints it.

missing.description: Missing is, for each package, what its tests skipped for lacking.

os.description: OS is the operating system the run's go test ran on (GOOS).

package_seconds.description: PackageSeconds is how long each package's tests took.

packages.description: Packages are the import paths the run tested.

schema.description: Schema is the run record's version (RunSchema).

seconds.description: Seconds is how long the run took.

skips.description: Skips are each test the run skipped, with its reason.

started.description: Started is when the run began.

verdict.description: Verdict is pass, fail, error (the run reached no verdict) or not-run. Known values: pass, fail, error, not-run. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

RunFailure.description: RunFailure is one failure, as go test reported it and as the run judged it.

kind.description: Kind is test, build or package (FailureKind). Known values: test, build, package. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

outcome.description: Outcome is failed, contention (it passed when re-run alone, so it does not count against the run) or not-rerun. Known values: failed, contention, not-rerun. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

output.description: Output is the end of what the test and its subtests printed (FailureOutput), masked by the caller.

package.description: Package is the failing package's import path.

test.description: Test is empty for a package-level failure.

Skip.description: Skip is one test go test reported as skipped, with the reason the test gave.

package.description: Package is the skipped test's import path.

reason.description: Reason is the first line of the message its skip gave, masked.

test.description: Test is the skipped test's name.

Step.description: Step is the record of one step pr-check ran besides the tests (govulncheck, the coverage check, the served-images check): how it exited, or why it did not run.

at.description: At is when the step's record was written; the zero time on a record from before steps carried one.

clean.description: Clean is true when the working tree had no uncommitted changes as pr-check began (prreport step -clean yes).

commit.description: Commit is the commit pr-check began at (prreport step -commit); absent on a record nobody stamped, which a merge cannot tie to any commit.

exit_code.description: ExitCode is how the step's command exited; 0 for a step that did not run.

kind.description: Kind is always step. Known values: step. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

name.description: Name is the step's name, which is also its record's file name.

reason.description: Reason is why a step with the not-run verdict did not run.

schema.description: Schema is the step record's version (StepSchema).

verdict.description: Verdict is pass, fail, or not-run for a step this machine could not make, which is said and not failed. Known values: pass, fail, not-run. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

description: Report is a pr-check run's records merged into one document with one verdict. Compatibility: schema is the major version, raised only by a change an existing reader could misread (a field removed or renamed, or given another type or meaning). Within a major version a newer producer may add fields, and values to the open sets; a reader ignores a field it does not know, treats a verdict, outcome or step it does not know as not a pass, and refuses a major version it does not know.

commit.description: Commit is the commit the run checked.

exit_code.description: ExitCode is pr-check's own exit status, the gate, when the merge was given it. A report never passes a run the gate failed.

expected.description: Expected is every part of the run pr-check said, as it began, it would run: passes, legs and steps by name.

generated.description: Generated is when this document was written.

kind.description: Kind is always pr-check. Known values: pr-check. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

legs.description: Legs are the OS checks' legs, in the order pr-check runs them.

missing.description: Missing is each expected part with no record, which is never a pass.

oldest.description: Oldest is when the oldest record in the report began: the earliest start of a pass or a leg, or time a step was written, a check with no machine set up left out. It is earlier than Started when make pr-check LEGS=... kept records from an earlier run, and the receipt's age is counted from it, so a reused govulncheck answer cannot outlive its advisory database. Absent when no record says when it began.

passes.description: Passes are the testgate passes on this machine, in the order pr-check runs them.

problems.description: Problems are each reason the report cannot simply be read as its records say.

schema.description: Schema is the report's major version.

started.description: Started is when pr-check began; absent when it wrote no running report first.

steps.description: Steps are the other steps, in the order pr-check runs them.

verdict.description: Verdict is the run's: pass, fail, incomplete (nothing failed, and something cannot be read as a pass), running (pr-check has begun and not ended: not a result) or interrupted (it stopped before its end). Known values: pass, fail, incomplete, running, interrupted. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

title: Pleiades pr-check report
